findings.title: Plan approval by the Load control lead is documented but never mentioned in practice
findings.text: SOP LC-07 §3.2 and the Load control lead's job description say the Load control lead approves the load plan before release to Ramp. The interview never mentions this approval.

evidence.quote: The preliminary load plan shall be approved by the Load Control Lead before release to Ramp
Accountable for approval of load plans

findings.title: Loading report return: 10 minutes in SOP RP-02, up to 15 minutes' wait in practice
findings.text: SOP RP-02 §2 has the Ramp Supervisor return the loading report within 10 minutes of loading completion; the Load controller says they sometimes wait fifteen minutes for it.

evidence.quote: return the loading report to Load Control within 10 minutes of loading completion
We sometimes wait fifteen minutes for it

findings.title: Weight-deviation decision: the Load control lead in SOP LC-07, the Captain in practice
findings.text: SOP LC-07 §5 has the Load Control Lead decide on corrective action when weights deviate beyond the airline tolerance; in practice the captain decides. The job descriptions are silent.

evidence.quote: the Load Control Lead shall decide on corrective action
it's the captain who decides, not us

findings.title: Loading report: sent within ten minutes officially, read at the aircraft on a busy wave
findings.text: Officially the Ramp sends the loading report within ten minutes; on a busy wave the Load controller walks down and reads it off the Ramp's sheet instead.

evidence.quote: Officially the ramp should send the report within ten minutes
What actually happens on a busy wave is I walk down and read it off their sheet

findings.title: Weight-deviation call: a fixed decider in SOP LC-07 for work the Load controller describes as having no fixed answer
findings.text: SOP LC-07 §5 sets who decides on corrective action when weights deviate; the Load controller describes it as a call with no fixed answer, where you read the situation.

evidence.quote: the Load Control Lead shall decide on corrective action

findings.basis: The Load controller says there is no fixed answer and that you read the situation, which marks the call as complex work rather than a set rule.

findings.title: Offload resolution is undocumented work
findings.text: When something can't be accepted, the airline decides what to offload, which takes fifteen to forty minutes before the Load controller re-plans. No SOP or job description covers it.

evidence.quote: If something can't be accepted, the airline decides what to offload

unknowns.question: Is the load plan approved by the Load control lead before release to Ramp, and if not, why not?
